summary.name: Vortex
summary.one_liner: Vortex is a free, open-source macOS notch app combining a focus timer, clipboard history, a file shelf for builds, screen-to-task capture with OCR, a keyboard-cleaning lock, and a keychain-backed key store that Claude Code can use without seeing the values.
use_cases: Keep a focus timer visible in the notch while working
Recover recently copied text, links, images or files
Collect new iOS or Android build files for upload
Capture bug reports from screen with app and page context
Let Claude Code run commands with API tokens without seeing them
Lock the keyboard while cleaning it
summary.what_it_does: Vortex opens from the MacBook notch on hover, or under the menu bar on Macs without a notch. The timer counts down from 1 to 120 minutes and sends a notification when it ends. Clipboard history keeps the last ten copies plus pins, and skips apps you exclude. The shelf holds files you drag in and can watch a build folder for new .ipa, .apk or .aab files. Screen tasks freeze the screen, save a cropped frame with app, window and page address, and run on-device OCR so search finds words in the image. Keys store secrets in the macOS keychain and let Claude Code run shell commands through a local MCP server, substituting values in as variables and removing them from output.
notable: Keys feature: Claude Code uses {{name}} placeholders so secrets stay out of its context, with per-key, per-session allow prompts
Offline by design: no analytics, update checks or accounts, and a build check blocks network code outside Keys
Shelf auto-catches fully written .ipa, .apk and .aab build files from watched folders
Modular architecture: each feature is a removable module
caveats: Requires macOS 14 or later and Apple silicon; Intel Macs are not supported
Not notarized by Apple, so macOS needs a manual Open Anyway step on first launch
Claude can still see command output, and secrets may leak via encoded output or other programs during command runs
